steps.text: Cook and stir sausage, beef, onion, and garlic in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat until browned; drain fat.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, and water until well combined.
Mix in sugar, basil, Italian seasoning, fennel seed, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until cooked through, about 1 ½ hours.
Serve with your favorite pasta and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: World’s Best Pasta Sauce!
raw_recipe.description: This pasta sauce is easy to make and great in lasagna or on your favorite pasta. It’s thick, hearty, and made with Italian sausage and ground beef.

review.reviewBody: I made this twice, first as written and it was GREAT! But then I did some mild modifications. I used all ground beef, addes red wine instead of water and added 1/2 tsp of oregano and rosemary plus 2 bay leaves. Put it in my crock pot for 4 hours and it was OUTSTANDING! I even had a true Italian guy tell me it was an outstanding sauce. I served it over spaghetti.

Awesome meat sauce!!! I sauteed the beef and sausage separately as they tend to be greasy and added them to the sauce during the last half hour of cooking. I then sauteed the onion with a little olive oil and garlic until translucent. I then added the tomatoes and spices. I used red wine vs. water, added 1/4 tsp. of red pepper flakes, doubled the basil, added 2 tsp. of oregano, and 1 bay leaf. The fennel seeds are a nice touch! This sauce was so good and tasted even better the next day.

I started making this sauce a few months ago. Since then, I absolutely REFUSE to buy any at the store. I love to add in fresh tomatoes from our garden, but even without it, this sauce KICKS tail. If I learned how to put it up in jars, I'd keep it on hand all the time. It makes a ton, and it is the single best sauce I have ever eaten.

I have been making this recipe for a long time now. It is excellent. Over time I made a few changes that perfect this recipe! 1) Add more garlic! You really can't put in too much! 2) Substitute a dry red wine for half of the the water. 3) Add 4-6 chopped fresh basil leaves! You'll love the aroma in the kitchen, and be amazed at how it affects the taste of the sauce. 4) Add about 1/2 tsp of oregano, and 1 bay leaf. Amazing pasta sauce!

I added one half cup small diced green peppers in addition to the half cup onion. I sauteed the green peppers and onion in a little olive oil until translucent, then added to the sauce. I used hot italian sausage instead of sweet (the tomato sauce hides the spicy and it just ends up being more flavorful than just sweet sausage) I add a little more garlic , and just be careful when adding salt because the sausage is already salty. I used 1/2 cup wine. Turned out AMAZING. Thank you :)

Very good pasta sauce. I made the following changes/additions. I used Marzano whole canned tomatoes instead of crushed. I crushed them myself with a potato masher. I substituted brown sugar for white. I used 4 cloves of garlic instead of 2. I added 1 cup red wine instead of water. I added 1 cup sun-dried tomato pesto (Progresso) and used fresh basil and oregano instead of dried basil, fennel seed and italian seasoning. My husband said this was the best pasta sauce he has ever had, and we eat italian food quite often.

First of all, the recipe is NOT 16 servings. I made it for 5 people, 2 of whom were seniors, and we barely had any leftovers. I followed the directions exactly the first time I made it, and made the following changes the second. It’s better!! When you buy the sausage it may come in an 18oz package. Slice it up and dump it all into a slow cooker. Your ground beef will come in a 1lb package. Dump it all into a slow cooker. Dice a small onion and add to the slow cooker. Pre-browning the meats/onion is not necessary. Add the tomato ingredients and water and stir well to loosen the ground beef. Cook on low for 8 hours. Double all of the spices on this recipe EXCEPT the sugar (I used garlic powder instead of fresh garlic) and add to the slow cooker at the 6 hour mark.
Great sauce. Only recommendation is to crush the fennel seed using a mortar and pestle before adding it to the sauce.

I increased the garlic to 5Tbsp, beef to 3lbs used 1 cup instead of 1/2 and used 2 packages of sweet sausage. (Do not pre-cook meats.) 
 The recipe is amazing, It fed my family of 7 and gave me 4 quarts of leftover sauce. 
 I plated it with garlic bread, 0.5lbs of a quality Linguini and freshly shaved parmesan cheese. 

P.S. I used french bread and a garlic spread for the GB. & topped it with a lite dusting of Italian seasoning.

It’s such a great recipe! I am usually a “feel” cook. Add a little of this and that to adjust the flavor to my family’s tastes. I used a combination of fresh basil and Italian seasoning with dried, a few bay leaves (2- 4 )and of course more fennel. A sprinkle of red pepper flakes. I added 1 pound ground pork and 1 1/2 pounds ground beef. Higher grade ingredients always makes a higher level of flavor. I use the cento brand which has a really great flavor. Really great recipe! Thanks so much for sharing! My family loves it! I also made her lasagna with this sauce and it was out of this world!!

Really great, I've made it twice and a few adjustments for a spicy version

- double or triple the fresh garlic
- broke up 1lb of spicy Andouille sausage, no beef
- initially threw in red pepper flakes in olive oil to cook with garlic, sausage and onion
- no water, no sugar
- added a couple bay leaves

Great recipe but I made a few tweaks. Instead of the minced onion bit I added three sweet onions, two bell peppers, and of course mushrooms. I tripled the amount of garlic. I added red wine instead of water. I added three tablespoons of sugar. I used 1 and 1/2 tablespoons of fresh basil instead of the dry stuff. I also added half a teaspoon of oregano, one bay leaf, and a teaspoon of Tony's.
Delicious!
I omitted the water and it was still saucy enough for me. Great flavors and a staple in my household!
I followed the tweaks made by Lindam748, and it was very tasty. Making so much is a challenge when cooking for 1 or 2 people.

The spices, garlic and onion Must be sauteed in heated olive oil first, then the Hamburg added. Meanwhile, the sausage Must be baked in the oven @ 350 F for 30 minutes, then sliced and added to the mixture that is sauteing. Let the mixture saute for an hour, then add tomato paste and tomatoes. Sauce must saute for a minimum of 2 hours. That is the way it is done.
World's best!
I have made this too many times to count! Sometimes I sub red wine for the water and add bay leaf. A meat lovers dream!
Love this recipe. Easy and great! Added more herbs like fresh basil and dried oregano. Worked grt
